name: Legal equivalence

subjectOf.text: The benefits of coding existing law into smart contracts are only temporary, because as smart contracting evolves over time fewer smart contracting solutions will have a real world equivalent.
subjectOf.abstract: The benefits of this hybrid approach are only temporary. As smart contracting evolves over time, fewer smart contracting solutions will have a real-world equivalent.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962
scope_conditions: over the course of smart contracting's evolution

subjectOf.text: Dual integration, as the authors define it, is the use of legacy legal infrastructure in smart contracting dispute resolution, such as Ricardian contracts, in combination with intra-blockchain systems for resolving smart contract disputes.
subjectOf.abstract: Dual integration refers to the use of legacy legal infrastructure in smart contracting dispute resolution, such as via the Ricardian contracts, among other measures, in combination with intra-blockchain systems for the resolution of smart contract disputes.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962
scope_conditions: the implementation and transition phase of the crypto economy

subjectOf.text: For crypto economy participants who wish to minimize the transaction costs of dual integration and retain anonymity, the authors' proposed open source platform ecosystem is more likely than all other available solutions to provide legal equivalence of dispute resolution mechanisms.
subjectOf.abstract: For participants in the crypto economy who wish to minimize the transaction costs of dual integration and retain anonymity, our proposed open source platform ecosystem is more likely than all other available solutions to provide legal equivalence of dispute resolution mechanisms.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962
scope_conditions: participants who want both low transaction costs and continuing anonymity
